clue.text: Grandeur may include something ludicrous

indicators.note: to include is to hold inside, so one word goes within the other here

parts.note: taken as written
a jest is a joke, something laughable

explanation.surface: Splendour can sometimes have a ridiculous side to it.
explanation.definitionFit: Majesty is stately splendour, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Queensland in Australia?

parts.note: read as 'a queen's land', the clue asks for an Australian state named after a British monarch, not the state actually called Queensland

explanation.definitionFit: This Australian state takes its name from the queen who reigned when it was founded, so it is literally a queen's land.

clue.text: Crazy type of fellow — 1 ac

parts.note: a fellow is a man
the Roman numeral for one is I
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dictionary-style gloss describing a madman.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunatic or madman is a crazy type of person.

clue.text: Set price destabilising income

indicators.note: destabilising upsets an arrangement, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fixed price is upsetting someone's earnings.
explanation.definitionFit: Receipts are the money taken in by a business, its income.

clue.text: Battle cut short by savoury tactics?

indicators.note: something cut short loses its tail, so the last letter goes

parts.note: Salamis was a sea battle of 480 BC between Greeks and Persians

explanation.surface: An ancient battle curtailed by a strategy of nibbling away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Salami tactics' is a strategy of gaining ground slice by slice; the question mark flags the sausage as the savoury source of that phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a savoury sausage that lends its name to salami tactics, gaining ground slice by slice.

clue.text: Study the benefit as comfort in bereavement

parts.note: to con is an old word for to study or learn
the dole is British slang for state unemployment benefit

explanation.surface: Learning that state benefits serve as consolation to the grieving.
explanation.definitionFit: To condole is to express sympathy with someone grieving, offering them solace.

clue.text: Monstrous character holding a party in jail

indicators.note: holding means one piece contains the other

parts.note: can is slang for prison
Lib is short for Liberal, a political party

explanation.surface: A monster of a man keeps a rowdy gathering going behind bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Caliban is the monstrous slave in Shakespeare's The Tempest.

clue.text: Where for the French it's part of 7

definitions.text: Where for the French it's part of 7

parts.words: Where for the French it's part of 7
parts.note: the place is a country whose French name, Liban, sits inside the letters of the 7 across answer

explanation.walkthrough: The French call this Middle Eastern country Le Liban, and LIBAN runs inside cALIBAN, the answer to 7 across.
explanation.definitionFit: The country's French name, Liban, can be found running inside the name of Shakespeare's monster.

clue.text: Infantry?

parts.note: read not as foot soldiers but as a collection of infants, carried rather than armed

explanation.definitionFit: Very young children still carried around, here pictured as an army of infants.

clue.text: That one seen at church with crumpled suit

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

indicators.note: a crumpled suit has lost its shape, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A man spotted at a service wearing a creased suit.
explanation.walkthrough: CESTUI is a legal term from Anglo-French, as in 'cestui que trust', the beneficiary of a trust.
explanation.definitionFit: In old legal French the term literally means he or that person, the beneficiary.

clue.text: City set in a river

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
laid means set down, placed

explanation.surface: A town placed in the middle of a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: Adelaide is the state capital of South Australia.

clue.text: It may give direction to a sailor

definitions.text: It may give direction to a sailor

parts.words: It may give direction to a sailor
parts.note: a heavenly body used in navigation, like the pole one guiding mariners by night

explanation.definitionFit: Sailors navigated by celestial bodies such as the pole one, which points north.

clue.text: Frisky racehorse reported in Wales

indicators.note: reported means spoken, so the words are heard, not spelt

parts.note: a young female horse that capers is a frisky filly, a caper filly

explanation.surface: A lively horse is spotted in Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: Caerphilly is a town in south Wales, also famous for its cheese.

clue.text: Letwin takes off as a celebrity

indicators.note: off means out of order or awry, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written; Oliver Letwin is a British politician
taken as written

explanation.surface: A politician named Letwin rises to fame.
explanation.definitionFit: She is a famous film actress, star of Titanic, so a celebrity.

clue.text: Network Rail's inner workings?

parts.note: Network Rail runs Britain's railway track; read whimsically, its guts are a pun on its name, the net plus rails reshuffled into innards

explanation.definitionFit: The innards or guts of a body are its inner workings in a humorous sense.

clue.text: Writer of various works, including one coming out

indicators.note: including means one piece holds another inside it

parts.note: Ralph Waldo Emerson, American essayist and poet
the Roman numeral for one is I

explanation.surface: An author of many works whose output includes a single piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Emersion is the act of emerging, rising out of water or into view.

clue.text: Delayed periodical rejection of a reproductive cell

parts.note: late means delayed
a mag, short for magazine, is a periodical

explanation.definitionFit: A gamete is a reproductive cell, so gametal is the adjective relating to one.

clue.text: Grass comprises part of land use, but not all

indicators.note: using only some of the letters of these words shows the answer is concealed inside them

explanation.surface: Grass makes up only a portion of how land is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Esparto is a tough grass of Spain and North Africa used for paper and rope.

clue.text: American trade balance before getting protection from falling

indicators.note: before places the first piece ahead of the next

parts.note: bal. is the accounting abbreviation for balance
taken as written

explanation.surface: A US trade surplus or deficit arrives first, before safeguards against a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A balustrade is a railing on posts that stops people falling off a balcony or stair.

clue.text: Arbiter amends premium with final reduction

indicators.note: amends means alters, so the remaining letters are rearranged
reducing at the end removes the last letter of the word premium

explanation.surface: A referee revises an insurance premium, trimming it at the end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with final reduction' drops the last M of PREMIUM, and 'amends' rearranges PREMIU.
explanation.definitionFit: An umpire is an arbiter who rules on disputes, in sport or otherwise.

clue.text: Tirade makes one scared head is for the chop

indicators.note: to chop the head off means the first letter goes

parts.note: someone scared is fearful

explanation.surface: A frightened person facing execution launches into a rant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head is for the chop' removes F from FEARFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: An earful is a long angry telling-off, a tirade.

clue.text: Grades said to be attainable with no difficulty

parts.note: E is an exam grade, so Es are grades

explanation.surface: Exam marks are reported to be easily achieved.
explanation.definitionFit: Ease is freedom from difficulty or effort.

clue.text: Plan some form of morbid new growth

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Arranging some sort of unhealthy growth.
explanation.definitionFit: A neoplasm is a tumour, an abnormal new growth of tissue.

clue.text: Pink and gold found in the Windward Islands

parts.note: rose is a pink colour
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Pink and gold treasure turning up in the Caribbean.
explanation.definitionFit: Roseau is the capital of Dominica, one of the Windward Islands of the Caribbean.

clue.text: Bush's battle honours?

definitions.meaning: a laurel is an evergreen bush, so these are such bushes
a wreath of bay leaves crowned victors, so the leaves stand for glory won

explanation.definitionFit: Laurel is an evergreen shrub whose leaves crowned victors, so the word also means honours won.

clue.text: Garment is fetching, revealing all within

indicators.note: within puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: fetching means attractive, cute
the lot means everything, all

explanation.surface: A fetching dress shows everything underneath.
explanation.definitionFit: A culotte is a divided skirt, a type of garment cut like wide trousers.
